defects.defect: Arithmetic/date error: trust periods expiring during calendar 1931 extended 'for a period of 10 years' run to dates in calendar 1941, so the latest possible end is 1941-12-31 (inclusive; exclusive reading would be the start of that day), not 1938-12-31. The claimed outer bound 'no part could run past 1938-12-31' is wrong.
Gap 3 repeats the wrong bound ('only the 1938-12-31 outer bound is claimed'); internally inconsistent with the order's own 1931 + 10-year term.
Ending bound not stated with the inclusive reading and exclusive alternative required by the 2026-10-21 'until' ruling.
Minor: both quotes match the held bytes only after whitespace normalisation (source has line breaks after 'expires' and 'period'); not verbatim byte substrings.
Limit (not by itself fatal outside the kit): no TERM:/ACT: evidence record, no acceptable_as_original source, material_gaps non-empty, approved false; the kit's _decision_errors would refuse it.

rationale: Identity, date and the single command are confirmed from two non-original held texts (government printed copy and 1974 OFR compilation OCR). The command is a one-time, fixed-term extension: each covered trust period expired at some date in 1931 and was extended 10 years, so the extension ended by its own terms on a date in 1941, at latest 1941-12-31 inclusive. No command survives to 2026-10-14 and Cruden finds no later instrument, so 'no' is substantively right. The proposal is still rejected because its stated outer bound (1938-12-31), which it repeats in the gaps, is wrong by three years. That is an error in the date of the ending basis. It also omits the inclusive/exclusive statement the 'until' ruling requires. Both texts are transcriptions: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved.
